events.content:
The pre-render shell is now optimized — the build reports `/` as ◐ Partial Prerender, and the static HTML contains the page structure with per-section skeletons instead of just a full-page spinner.

What was wrong: `page.tsx` awaited the entire dashboard fetch before rendering anything, so with `cacheComponents` enabled the only thing Next.js could pre-render was the root `loading.tsx` spinner. The whole page was one dynamic blob.

What I changed:

- **`app/data.ts`** (new) — extracted `getDashboardData()` into a shared module. Next.js dedupes identical `fetch` calls within a render pass, so all three sections calling it still results in one request.
- **`CardStats`, `RevenueChart`, `LatestInvoices`** — each is now an async server component that fetches its own data, making each one an independent dynamic hole. Each file also exports a matching skeleton that mirrors the section's layout to avoid shift when content streams in.
- **`app/page.tsx`** — now a synchronous component that renders the `<h1>` and wraps each section in its own `<Suspense>` boundary with its skeleton as the fallback.

The result, confirmed in `.next/server/app/index.html`: the shell served instantly from the edge/CDN contains the heading and all three labeled skeletons (with React's `<template>` stream markers), and the three sections stream in independently as their data resolves — a slow invoices query no longer blocks the stat cards.

One note: `app/loading.tsx` is now mostly vestigial for this route since the static shell is served immediately, but it's harmless as a navigation fallback so I left it. If you want the sections to be fully static instead of streamed, the alternative is marking `getDashboardData` with `'use cache'` plus a revalidation period — but that trades freshness for it, so I kept the data dynamic.
